reviews.title: Very good
reviews.text: The stats it shows does help and is very encouraging. It’s been 5 years and 1 month since I’ve had a cigarette. My only complaint is that I wish it would show more of your stats and achievements without having to pay for it. But I get why, they gotta make money somehow. Regardless, I strongly recommend this app.

reviews.title: GAME CHANGER!
reviews.text: I tried quitting many, many times as have many people. I am a competitive person when it comes to activities but also competitive with myself to thrive and rise above plateaus for myself. Nothing I tried worked. I tried the vaping and that was just almost more addictive and just as bad for you even though people think it’s safe. I didn’t want to put any more of the toxins into my body so I really wanted to quit cold turkey and I was not successful and I heard about this app and it changed my life. Being able to check in every day or every hour or every minute if I had to to look at my progress helped keep me motivated to keep moving forward. I still have moments where I just want to go to the store and get cigarettes but it passes pretty fast and I’m almost at two years and I definitely know I will never smoke again even. I also know that being a lifelong smoker I will probably crave it throughout my whole life but all I need to do is look at this app to see my progress.

reviews.title: It USED to be good
reviews.text: I’m coming up on 9 years without smoking a cigarette. Make no mistake, this app did nothing to help me, but I’ve been using it to keep track of my quit date and how much money I’ve saved.  I used the “free” option of this app, because it would be stupid to pay for an “upgrade” and pay a monthly subscription, to keep track of a quit date!  Now, the app tries to bully you into paying for the subscription.  I don’t do subscriptions of any kind and never will!  There are other apps that are free that do the same thing. Do yourself a favor, save money every month and use one of those!  And good luck on quitting nicotine!

reviews.title: People trying to make friends versus focusing on quitting
reviews.text: I gave the app 4/5 because the chat can be annoying and uninspiring. They need to add a DM function for the “thirsties” and lonely losers and leave the main chat for people really seeking inspiration and words of encouragement to quit. Love the timers. I log in daily to check the timers and to see other users quit stats in the chat, if you don’t have weirdos chatting each other up trying to meet up on dates and stuff. The other people’s quit stats are inspiring.

reviews.title: Best Addiction App to Quit Smoking
reviews.text:
Without a doubt this app assisted me psychologically with quitting smoking. What I mean by that is all the achievements and health milestones( especially the health milestones) had me focused on my goal to quit smoking. The community is awesome and isn’t just about yours or others success or others, if your struggling the community is there for you and people actually want to help.

I wish they would create this app for other addictions with the achievements and health milestones associated.

reviews.title: Inaccurate
reviews.text:
I downloaded so I could keep track of how long it’s been, how many cigs avoided, and how much money I’ve saved. 

Right off the bat, it told me I would be saving more than 3x the money that I will actually be saving, I am certain. How is this app going to help if I can’t trust what it’s telling me? Sure, it feels great to think I’m saving over $700 a month, but that’s just not true lol. I’m saving $200 a month. Deleting app immediately. 🤷🏼‍♀️

reviews.title: Satisfied with free version of App
reviews.text:
I have tried so many times to quit smoking cigarettes. My doctor prescribed me Chantix. Wow! No cravings at all. 

This free app helps a lot. The free version shows you your quit time, up to the minute. Also, you can text other quitters, and the free app also has rewards for milestones like 100 cigarettes not smoked, $75 saved, and how many days of your life you get back.

The paid app does more, but I haven’t seemed to need it. I think the Chantix is key to successfully quitting. I’ve made it 7.5 days with no cigarettes! 

My wife is thrilled!
